chunks: The chief of al-Jalut said to the Jews: 'The Muslims claim that Ali (peace be upon him) is among the most skilled in argumentation and the most knowledgeable of the people. Let us go to him so that I may ask him a question and make him err in it.'
So he came to him and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I want to ask you a question.' He said: 'Ask about whatever you wish.' He said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, when was our Lord?'

He said to him: 'O Jew, it is only said "when was he" about one who did not exist and then came to be. As for when He was — He was existing without there being any entity. He was existing without a "how" coming to be. Yes, O Jew! Then again, yes, O Jew! How can there be a "before" for Him? He is before the "before" without there being an end-point, and no termination of an end-point, nor is there an end-point that leads to it. The end-points cease at His presence. He is the end-point of every end-point.'
So he said: 'I testify that your religion is the Truth and that whatever opposes it is false.'

key_terms.رَأْسُ الْجَالُوت: Exilarch — The head of the Jewish Diaspora community, a title used in the Islamic period for the leader of the Jewish community under Muslim rule
key_terms.غَايَة: End-point, limit, or goal — The hadith employs this term repeatedly to convey that God transcends all limits and is Himself the ultimate endpoint of all things
key_terms.كَيْنُونِيَّة: Modality of being/entity — Imam Ali uses this rare philosophical term to deny that God came into existence in any manner; He was always existing without becoming so
key_terms.مَتَى كَانَ: The temporal question 'when was he?' — Only applicable to contingent beings; inapplicable to God who is eternal

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say when asked 'when was God?' by the Jewish exilarch?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a remarkable theological exchange in which the Jewish exilarch Ra's al-Jalut, seeking to embarrass Imam Ali (AS) with a philosophical trap about God's temporality, is instead confronted with a profound articulation of divine transcendence. Imam Ali responds by demolishing the very presupposition of the question: the question 'when was God?' only applies to contingent beings that came into existence, whereas God exists beyond time, before any concept of 'before', beyond any limiting category of 'how' or 'when'. The exilarch, overwhelmed by the clarity and depth of this response, embraces Islam. This hadith reflects the early Shia tradition of 'ilm al-kalam (theological discourse) and showcases Imam Ali's role as the supreme interpreter of Islamic theology, especially regarding divine attributes and God's relationship to time.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Amro Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Sama’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Chief Al-Jalout said to the Jews that the Muslims are alleging that Ali<sup>asws</sup> is from the best of the people in the art of argumentation and their most knowledgeable. Let us go to him<sup>asws</sup>. I shall ask him<sup>asws</sup> a question and make him<sup>asws</sup> err in it’.

So he came over to himasws and he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! I wanted to ask youasws a question’. Heasws said: ‘Ask about whatever you so desire to’. He said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! When was our Lordazwj (from)?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘O Jew! But rather, it is said, ‘When was he’, for the one who did not happen to be. So He<sup>azwj</sup> was when He<sup>azwj</sup> was. He<sup>azwj</sup> was existing without there being any entity. He<sup>azwj</sup> exists without a ‘how’ (Qualitative State) happening to be.  
Yes, O Jew! Then (again), yes O Jew! How can there be a ‘before’ for Him<sup>azwj</sup>? He<sup>azwj</sup> was before the ‘before’, without there being an end-point and no termination of an end-point, nor is there an end-point having a termination to it. The end-point is in His<sup>azwj</sup> Presence. He<sup>azwj</sup> is the end-point of all end-points’.
So he said, ‘I testify that your<sup>asws</sup> Religion is the Truth and that whatever is different to it, is false’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ’Amr ibn ’Uthman from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Suma‘ah from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), who has said the following. “Ra’sul Jalut said to the Jews, ‘The Muslims consider Ali excelling everyone in polemics and the most learned. Let us go to him. I will ask him certain questions and perhaps catch him in errors.’”

He went to the Imam (a.s.) and said, “O Amirul Mu’minin, I have a question about a matter.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Ask about whatever you like.” He then asked, “O Amirul Mu’minin, when did our Lord come into existence?”

Imam Ali replied, “O Jew, the question When applies to one who did not exist and (then) came into being. Allah has exists without coming into being, and without being in any becoming. Certainly, O Jew, most certainly, O Jew, how can there be any before for He Who was before the before. He does not have any destination. He is not the end of any destination and no destination ends up to Him. All destinations fall short before Him and He is the goal of all destinations.”
The Jew then said, “I testify that your religion is the true religion and any thing against it is false.”
